high.title: Central Bank Should Make Maximum Two 25-Point Cuts to Selic in 2026, Says Matheus Spiess from Empiricus Research
high.summary: The Central Bank should implement at most one or two 25 basis point cuts to the Selic rate before pausing the easing cycle, according to Empiricus Research strategist Matheus Spiess. This dovish outlook comes as IPCA-15 inflation data for May came in above expectations at 0.62% monthly (vs. 0.57% expected), with the 12-month accumulated rate reaching 4.64% - above the BCB's 4.5% inflation target ceiling. Spiess noted that the composition of recent inflation prints is concerning, particularly the 1.36% monthly increase in food and beverages prices. The above-target inflation reading reduces room for aggressive monetary easing and supports a more cautious approach from COPOM. For BRL traders, this suggests the BCB may pause rate cuts sooner than expected, which could provide some support for the Real. Bond investors should expect limited duration gains as the easing cycle appears to be nearing its end, with yields likely to stabilize at current levels if inflation remains persistently above target.

high.title: Ibovespa Has Longest Weekly Losing Streak Since 2004 and Braskem (BRKM5) Leads Negative Side
high.summary: The Ibovespa extended its losing streak to seven consecutive weeks, the longest decline since 2004, falling 1.37% for the week to close at 173,787.49 points. The prolonged selloff reflects uncertainties over Middle East conflicts and domestic political risks weighing on Brazilian equities. USD/BRL gained 0.29% for the week, closing at R$5.0429, indicating continued pressure on the Real amid risk-off sentiment. The above-target IPCA-15 inflation reading of 4.64% annually (vs. 4.5% target ceiling) added to concerns about monetary policy constraints. Political uncertainty remains central to investor concerns, contributing to the sustained equity outflows. The seven-week decline matches the longest streak seen in April-May 2004, highlighting the severity of current market pessimism. For international fund managers, this presents both risks from continued political volatility and potential opportunities as valuations become more attractive.

medium.title: Durigan Says US Designation of Criminal Factions as Terrorists Could Affect Economy
medium.summary: Finance Minister Dario Durigan warned that the US designation of Brazil's two largest criminal factions as terrorist organizations could impact the economy and put foreign investments at risk. Durigan also defended Brazil's PIX payment system, calling it "the greatest symbol of Brazil's financial sovereignty," amid concerns it could be targeted as potentially facilitating organized crime. This geopolitical development could create additional headwinds for BRL and Brazilian assets if it affects investor sentiment about security and regulatory risks.
